occupational exposure risks to monoclonal antibody and fusion protein therapies have not been formally evaluated and evidence-based guidance is urgently required to direct safe handling of novel anticancer agents in a variety of clinical practice settings.

the safe handling of novel anticancer agents, specifically monoclonal antibodies and fusion proteins.
the development of a framework to evaluate occupational exposure risk to novel anticancer therapies.
the occupational risks associated with the handling of novel anticancer agents, particularly monoclonal antibodies and fusion proteins.

there is insufficient evidence to make a definitive statement on the occupational exposure risk for the majority of novel agents.
there is insufficient evidence to determine the occupational exposure risks to these agents.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evidence for occupational risks from monoclonal antibodies and other novel anticancer agents are limited and yet to formally evaluated.
the occupational risks of novel agents are unknown.
the evidence base for the safe handling and occupational exposure risks of novel agents is limited.
The main takeaway from our work is that
occupational exposure risks to monoclonal antibody agents have not been formally evaluated from the perspective of the Australian healthcare system.
the risk to healthcare personnel from exposure to novel anticancer drugs has not been adequately assessed.
there are a lack of evidence-based guidelines for the occupational exposure risks for novel anticancer drugs, including monoclonal antibodies and other biologic agents.
